events.description:
All are welcome to attend the Theater Department’s performances of Bakersfield Mist by Stephen Sachs, directed by Peter Hansen, and performed by St. Olaf students.

Maude, a fifty-something unemployed bartender, has bought a painting for a few bucks from the thrift store. Despite almost trashing it, she now thinks it’s a Jackson Pollock worth millions. But when world-class art expert, Lionel Percy, flies over from New York and arrives at her trailer park home in Bakersfield to authenticate the painting, he has no idea what he is about to discover. Inspired by true events, this sparkling and colorful new comedy-drama asks vital questions about what makes art and people truly authentic.
events.title: St. Olaf Theatre Department Presents — Bakersfield Mist

The St. Olaf Cantorei Choir, conducted by Adjunct Instructor of Music Jon Madden, will perform in Boe Memorial Chapel on Sunday, October 25, from 3:30-5:30 p.m.

The St. Olaf Cantorei was established in the 1960s as the Campus Choir to provide opportunities for more students to participate in the St. Olaf choral tradition. The ensemble has become known for creative programming that blends the St. Olaf choral tradition with instrumental color and is uniquely honed and focused to lead worship and provide a distinctive musical and spiritual experience.

events.description: The Buntrock Institute for Freedom and Community invites the greater campus community to their Fall Speaker Series featuring Lisa Tetrault, Associate Professor of History at Carnegie Mellon University, who will present When Women Won the Right to Vote: An American Fiction on October 29 from 3:45-4:45 p.m. in Viking Theater. The lecture will discuss how when women won passage of the Nineteenth Amendment in 1920, they did not win the right to vote. Contrary to popular assumption, the right to vote does not exist in the US Constitution. Just what, then, did the woman suffrage amendment accomplish?  Clarifying this history, this talk positions 1920 as the middle of a much larger story about the curious — and largely unknown — absence of a constitutional voting right for all Americans.

organizer.organizer: Buntrock Institute for Freedom and Community

events.title: When Women Won the Right to Vote:  An American Fiction

Imagine St. Olaf: Conversations for the Future

Hear directly from President Susan Rundell Singer and Kirsten Cahoon ’98, Director of the Piper Center for Vocation and Career, as they engage in conversation on “The St. Olaf Pathway and Internships.” Learn how St. Olaf equips students for meaningful careers—and how you can help shape their future through mentorship, expertise, and support.

Event details:

  • Date: Thursday, October 29, 2026
  • Time: 5:30 to 8:30 p.m. | Program at 6:30 p.m.
  • Location: Limelight Hotel (Kenosha Ballrooms), 1600 Wewatta St., Denver, CO 80202
  • Admission: Free of charge (includes beverages and heavy hors d’oeuvres)

Evening Schedule & Highlights

5:30 p.m. – Welcome Reception: Connect over drinks and heavy hors d’oeuvres with Denver-area Oles, parents, and St. Olaf leadership.

6:30 p.m. – Main Program & Q&A: Hosted by Joshua Lee (Associate Director of Alumni and Parent Relations) and moderated by Ana Hernandez ’94 (Alumni and Family Board Member), this interactive panel discusses how St. Olaf equips students for the future. Hear directly from President Susan Rundell Singer and Kirsten Cahoon ’98, Director of the Piper Center for Vocation and Career.

Get Involved: Discover practical ways to stay engaged locally, support current students, and connect back on the Hill.

Um! Yah! Yah!

events.description:
The St. Olaf Festival of Bands, scheduled for October 31, 2026, has enjoyed a long, successful history of bringing together outstanding high school musicians to prepare and share a program with nationally acclaimed artists. An exciting and intense day of rehearsals culminates with performances by the Festival Band, the St. Olaf Band, and the Norseman Band. It promises to be a stimulating day for students and teachers alike.

We are excited to announce that guest clinician Lauren Reynolds will bring her exceptional expertise to lead the Festival Band this year. As associate professor of music and director of concert bands at the University of Delaware School of Music, where she conducts the wind ensemble and teaches conducting and wind literature, Dr. Reynolds is a distinguished leader in the field. Her participation promises to be an inspiring and invaluable experience for all involved.

We will also be joined by Michael Buck, conductor of the Norseman Band. Michael Buck is a 1989 graduate of St. Olaf College and the former director of bands at The College of St. Scholastica in Duluth. We are thrilled about the ongoing impact he is making on music-making at St. Olaf and the Festival of Bands.
events.title: St. Olaf Festival of Bands Concert
